Opposite ... on 18 May, 2023 Author: Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi Bench: Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi 1 In The High Court Of Jharkhand, Ranchi Cr. M.P. No.5 of 2011 Janardhan Mandal and Another ..... Petitioners Versus The State of Jharkhand .... Opposite Party ----- Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi ----- For the Petitioner : Mr. Sudhansu Kumar Deo, Advocate For the State : Mr. Sunil Kr. Dubey, A.P.P. ----- 10/18.05.2023 2. The petitioners are aggrieved by the order dated 23.09.2010 passed by learned Sessions Judge, Deoghar, in Cr. Revision No.85 of 2008, whereby the revision filed against the order dated 11.4.2008 passed by learned S.D.J.M., Deoghar, in G.O.C.R. Case No.52 of 2008, T.R. No.1531 of 2008, taking cognizance against the petitioner for the offence under Section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 has been dismissed by the Revisional Court below. 3. From the prosecution report it appears that the sample of Khowa was taken from the shop of the petitioner, which upon analysis by the Public Analyst was found to be adulterated.
texts.facts: 2. The petitioners are aggrieved by the order dated 23.09.2010 passed by learned Sessions Judge, Deoghar, in Cr. Revision No.85 of 2008, whereby the revision filed against the order dated 11.4.2008 passed by learned S.D.J.M., Deoghar, in G.O.C.R. Case No.52 of 2008, T.R. No.1531 of 2008, taking cognizance against the petitioner for the offence under Section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 has been dismissed by the Revisional Court below. 3. From the prosecution report it appears that the sample of Khowa was taken from the shop of the petitioner, which upon analysis by the Public Analyst was found to be adulterated. On the basis of the said report the cognizance was taken against the petitioner for the offence under Section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act. It appears from the later portion of the said order itself, that upon getting the notice of the result of the Public Analyst, the petitioner had exercised the option under Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act to get the sample tested before the Central Food Laboratory at Kolkata, and the said prayer was allowed by the Court below. 4. A short point has been taken by the learned counsel for the petitioners, submitting that as per Section 13(2D) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, until the result of the analysis from the Janardhan Mandal And Another vs The State Of Jharkhand .... Opposite ... on 18 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183361140/ 1 Director of the Central Food Laboratory was received, the Court could not proceed with the matter. Learned counsel accordingly, submitted that the impugned order taking cognizance against the petitioners cannot be sustained in the eyes of law.
texts.arguments: 5. Learned counsel for the State, on the other hand, has opposed the prayer submitting that the cognizance order has been passed on the basis of the analysis made by the Public Analyst and accordingly, there is no illegality in the matter. 6. Sections 13(2) and 13(2D) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act are reproduced below :- "13 Report of public analyst. - (2). On receipt of the report of the result of the analysis under sub-section (1) to the effect that the article of food is adulterated, the Local (Health) Authority shall, after the institution of prosecution against the persons from whom the sample of the article of food was taken and the person, if any, whose name, address and other particulars have been disclosed under Section 14A, forward, in such manner as may be prescribed, a copy of the report of the result of the analysis to such person or persons, as the case may be, informing such person or persons that if it is so desired, either or both of them may make an application to the Court within a period of ten days from the date of receipt of the copy of the report to get the sample of the article of food kept by the Local (Health) Authority analysed by the Central Food Laboratory. *** *** *** (2D).

On receipt of the report of the result of the analysis under sub-section (1) to the effect that the article of food is adulterated, the Local (Health) Authority shall, after the institution of prosecution against the persons from whom the sample of the article of food was taken and the person, if any, whose name, address and other particulars have been disclosed under Section 14A, forward, in such manner as may be prescribed, a copy of the report of the result of the analysis to such person or persons, as the case may be, informing such person or persons that if it is so desired, either or both of them may make an application to the Court within a period of ten days from the date of receipt of the copy of the report to get the sample of the article of food kept by the Local (Health) Authority analysed by the Central Food Laboratory. *** *** *** (2D).
